why: Removals cascade (removing one group can make a new group), which is exactly what a stack of (character, run length) handles: each character extends or starts the top run, and a run that reaches k is popped. It teaches the 'stack of (value, count)' technique.
hints: After a group of k is removed, which characters become neighbours? Where do you need to look to see whether a new group forms?
Only at the end of the text you have kept so far. Keep a stack of runs (char, count): an equal character increments the top count, a different one pushes (char, 1).
When the top count reaches k, pop it; the run below is now the top and the next equal character continues it. Rebuild the string from the runs. O(n).
pitfalls: Rescanning the string after every removal is O(n^2/k) and too slow for n = 10^5.
A stack of single characters cannot tell you the run length in O(1); store the count with the character.
